description: Dependency updates. Replaces .github/dependabot.yml — see ADR-0019 for why.
Renovate is self-hosted from .github/workflows/renovate.yml, not the GitHub App:
this file has to work unchanged on GitLab, and the App is GitHub-only.
IT DOES NOTHING UNTIL A RENOVATE_TOKEN SECRET EXISTS. That is a manual step in
the GitHub UI and is written down in docs/repository-setup.md.
Renovate config is JSON with no comment syntax, so every non-obvious rule below
carries a `description` — which is not decoration: Renovate prints them on the
Dependency Dashboard, so the reasoning shows up where the PR does. Only the keys
that accept one have it; the rest is explained here.
prHourlyLimit: the default is 2, sized for Renovate running hourly. This runs
weekly (the cron in renovate.yml), so 2 would mean two PRs a week and a backlog
that never drains. 0 removes the hourly limit; prConcurrentLimit (10, inherited
from config:recommended) is what actually bounds the queue — the same number
dependabot.yml used for open-pull-requests-limit.
postUpgradeTasks: closes the two-file bump. .devcontainer/.env and mise.lock are
one change split across two files — a bumped version with a stale lock has no
reviewed checksum, and `pnpm verify:mise` fails the PR for it. Renovate can only
edit the first file, so it runs the command a human would run, in the branch,
before the PR opens. That needs mise on PATH inside the Renovate container
(.github/renovate-entrypoint.sh) and the command allowed globally via
RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS in the workflow. If it fails, the PR still opens with a
stale lock and verify:mise catches it: the failure mode is a red PR you finish by
hand, not a lock nobody checked.
No `schedule` here on purpose. The workflow cron already decides when Renovate
runs, and a schedule in this file would also silently swallow manual
workflow_dispatch runs outside its window. No automerge either — every PR in this
repo is merged by a human.

devcontainer.description: Disabled deliberately. The authoritative pin for the docker-in-docker feature is the version+integrity pair in .devcontainer/devcontainer-lock.json, and Renovate cannot regenerate that lock. It would bump the `:4` selector in devcontainer.json and leave the lock resolving the old digest — a half-applied bump that still builds, from a lock nobody reviewed. Bump both by hand with `devcontainer upgrade`. See the comment on DOCKER_IN_DOCKER_FEATURE_VERSION in .devcontainer/.env.

mise.description: Disabled deliberately. mise.toml holds no versions — every value is a `{{ env.X }}` template resolved from .devcontainer/.env (ADR-0004). Renovate cannot read through the template, so leaving this manager on would list nine permanently-unresolvable dependencies on the dashboard. The real pins are reached by the customManager below.

customManagers.description: Version pins in .devcontainer/.env, matched by the `# renovate:` annotation written directly above each one. The annotation lives at the pin rather than in a datasource table here on purpose: it is readable by whoever is editing the pin, it survives a key rename, and a key with no annotation is visibly untracked — which is how JAVA_VERSION, the apt pins, the base image and the devcontainer feature advertise that they are bumped by hand, each with the reason stated in that file.

The gitleaks scanner image in the CI job. It is a `docker run` inside a `run:` block, not a `uses:` or a Dockerfile FROM, so no built-in manager sees it. Both halves of the pin are captured — currentValue is the tag `pnpm verify:mise` compares against GITLEAKS_VERSION, currentDigest is what actually gets pulled.

packageRules.description: Carried over from dependabot.yml: type packages move together. Listed before the `next` group so react's types can be claimed back by it below — later rules win in Renovate, where Dependabot took the first match.

gitleaks is the one tool pinned twice — GITLEAKS_VERSION in .devcontainer/.env drives the pre-commit hook, the tag+digest in security.yml drives CI, and scripts/verify-mise-lock.mjs asserts they are equal (ADR-0018). Ungrouped, Renovate would open two PRs that each pass on their own branch and fail the instant either one merged.

NODE_VERSION in .devcontainer/.env and .nvmrc are the same number in two files, reached by two different managers. Same for PYTHON_VERSION and scripts/.python-version. One PR each, or they drift for however long the second PR sits.

ESLint 10 removed context.getFilename(), which eslint-plugin-react still calls — it throws "contextOrFilename.getFilename is not a function" on any file containing a component. eslint-plugin-import and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y also cap their peer range at ^9. All three are already at their latest release, so there is nothing to upgrade *to*. Drop this rule once they ship ESLint 10 support.
@types/node must track the Node major actually being run (24 — see engines, mise.toml and the workflows), not npm's latest. A newer major type-checks against APIs that do not exist at run time.
